the molecular mechanisms that control the expression of major histocompatibility class I genes in a murine tumor cell line.
the molecular mechanisms that regulate the expression of major histocompatibility genes and their role in the development of tumors.
the molecular mechanism of class I down regulation in murine fibroblastic tumor cell lines.

the class I genes in the murine fibrosacoma IC9 are turned off by a mechanism at the level the chromatin structure, which results in the down regulation of these genes at the transcriptional level.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the class I deficiency in the fibrosarcoma line IC9 is not the result of a mutation or a deletion in the class I gene itself, but rather is the result of an epigenetic mechanism that prevents the class I gene from being transcribed.

the expression of the silent class-I genes in IC9 cells is turned off at the level of chromatin structure.
